entries.claim: Checker capacity: channel-count vs policy, isolated
entries.definition: [E] Separates channel-count from policy. Rows: 10-channel checker vs 5-channel RUN3 subset. Columns: hardening-probe baseline samples (SFT policy, 40 targets x 8, closed-book) vs RS-SFT's own samples (75 targets x 32, resampling_rate). Until this ran, '14% -> 27%' conflated two changes (fewer channels, different policy) -- this isolates each.
entries.note: r2_checker_capacity_rssft.json's own combined number for the same cell (5-channel RUN3 checker on RS-SFT's samples) is 26.75%, not this file's 26.69% -- 0.06pp apart despite byte-identical n_scored/n_parse_fail counts (1280/88 heldout, 1120/37 astral, confirmed in both scripts' run logs) and literally shared code (r1_r3 imports r2's own score_target_set + capacity_metrics by name rather than reimplementing them; neither function nor its dependencies changed in git between the two runs). ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND CONFIRMED this session, not merely two different pipelines: the gap is PYTHONHASHSEED-dependent. A controlled rerun of the identical pipeline with PYTHONHASHSEED pinned to 0 reproduces 26.75% (bit-identical per-channel z_var to r2's file); pinned to 1, it reproduces 26.69% exactly; this project's run scripts never pin PYTHONHASHSEED, so every separate process invocation samples a different (but internally consistent) hash seed. The validator's mp_formula_set membership test (line ~660, ~1149) does not depend on set iteration order, so it is not the mechanism; the exact hash-order-sensitive step inside validator.validate()'s thermodynamic/competing-phase scoring was not pinned down further here (out of scope for a housekeeping pass, and validator.py is the user's own file to edit) -- the controlled PYTHONHASHSEED=0-vs-1 test is sufficient to confirm the MECHANISM (hash-seed-dependent tie-breaking on a small number of borderline cases) without locating the specific line. Neither 26.75% nor 26.69% is 'more correct' -- both are the same code and data under two valid interpreter states. Quote 26.75% for the RS-SFT/5-channel cell (matching the separately-tracked r2_checker_capacity_rssft.json, so the two files agree), and pin PYTHONHASHSEED=0 in any future rerun of this pipeline for exact reproducibility. The table's other three cells are far less likely to be affected at a reportable precision -- the 10-channel checker's extra, mostly-dead channels make its covariance less sensitive to a handful of flipped ties -- but were not re-verified under both seeds here.

entries.claim: Hodge (gradient/curl/harmonic) decomposition of each reward's pairwise preference graph

channel_set_curl_prediction.ratio_diff_over_same: undefined -- same-channel-set curl is numerically zero (<1e-9); the entire curl signal is attributable to channel-set heterogeneity across the triangle's three comparisons

entries.definition: Checker/ranker are scalar-derived (curl-free by construction, a trivial control); R5 (the learned comparator, gate-wrapped as actually used downstream) is the real test for both exact antisymmetry (c(a,b)+c(b,a)=0) and curl-freeness (does preference around a 3-cycle sum to 0?).
entries.note: R5 shows ZERO antisymmetry violations on every ARROWS3 pool (necessary but not sufficient for a global ranking). Its curl is small but real (5.2% of ASTRAL's total preference energy) and traced to the pre-registered mechanism exactly: triangles where all three pairwise comparisons gate the same reward channels on/off have curl numerically zero (<1e-9); the curl signal sits entirely on channel-set-heterogeneous triangles (mean |curl| 0.268 vs ~0 when the channel set matches) -- channel-gating inconsistency, not a real intransitive preference. 17% of all triangles are the cyclic (C3) kind curl can even act on.

entries.note: The point estimates barely move (R4_ranker 11.55 -> 11.27pp); only the CI width changes, and only R4_ranker's verdict flips: [-13.89,29.40] (includes 0, 'no climb') becomes [1.88,20.62] (excludes 0, 'climbs'). This is the SAME CLASS OF BUG an earlier within-temperature pooling fix caught in Block R -- concatenating resample draws across a grouping dimension instead of averaging within each replicate first inflates the CI without moving the point estimate. Separately, the Goodhart best-of-n curve (n=1..16) turns down for R2_checker (classic overfitting to a proxy) but climbs monotonically for R4_ranker and R5_comparator over this range -- no turnover observed yet for those two, within n<=16.

entries.claim: Calibration of Block A's K=8-trace marginal pi~ estimator against real held-out frequency

value.nasrbo3_note: NaSrBO3: pi~_rs_sft=0.49242519 vs empirical rate 18/232=0.0776 across every RS-SFT sample on disk for this target (both the 32-sample resampling_rate draw AND the 200-sample reference pool). The estimator OVERSTATES the true rate by roughly 6.3x -- not the 'tails underestimated' direction regular Claude's hypothesis 2 predicted, the OPPOSITE: this specific cell is a case where the sparse 8-trace average happened to draw at least one trace assigning this recipe very high probability, and that one trace dominates the mean (log of an average of mostly-near-zero and one large value is pulled toward the large value). Not a canonicaliser or surface-form mismatch (checked: the exact predicted set does appear, hit rate ~7.76%, in both sample groups, so the key itself resolves correctly) -- an estimator-variance artifact specific to whichever traces happened to be among this target's up-to-8.

entries.definition: For every (model, target, recipe) cell where pi~ < 1e-4, sum the expected count (pi~ x n_held_out) and the observed count across all such cells, pooled; ratio = observed/expected.
entries.note: 7,425x pooled under-estimate; per-model <1e-6 bin ratios range 100,378x-1,724,611x. This single estimator feeds Block B1's c_s/d_s regression terms (signature.json) AND R-h's reachability denominator (audit_reach.json) AND, uncorrected, Block B3's leash overshoot -- the shared root cause behind most of the withdrawn 'practice reaches the unreachable' headline. NaSrBO3 is the one target where the estimator errs in the OPPOSITE direction (overstates by ~6.3x) -- a sparse-average variance artifact, not a canonicaliser bug (the predicted set does resolve correctly in both sample groups).

entries.claim: Block A: are the ASTRAL hit-rate 'replications' real, and is Phase 12's gain over RS-SFT noise?

value.replication_files_were_deterministic_rer: These two files (data/novelty/*.jsonl) are gitignored by the project's standing convention (data/ holds generation dumps, not tracked results). Recorded here by sha256 so the held-out legs' outputs are checkable without being committed.

entries.definition: hit-rate = targets where >=1 of 32 samples matches the ASTRAL rule-picked precursor set. Unpaired: bootstrap each model's own 32 draws/target independently. Paired: draw ONE set of resampled positions per target, apply to BOTH Phase12@300 and RS-SFT, so common per-target noise cancels in the diff rather than inflating the CI.
entries.note: The four *_replication.json ASTRAL legs reused seed=42 (astral_model_generations.py's default, never overridden) and are 1,120/1,120 samples byte-identical to the originals -- deterministic re-runs, not independent replications. The real sampling-noise read: Phase12@300's own interval [9,14] overlaps RS-SFT's [8,10] at 9-10 on an UNPAIRED bootstrap. PAIRED (same resampled positions, finding-22's actual comparison): median diff=2, 95% CI [-1,5] -- includes 0. Finding 22's '14/35 vs 10/35, consistent with amplification, not yet statistically decisive' is the correct framing and should carry this interval as its fragility caveat; this check neither proves nor overturns it.

entries.claim: Gate G1: median Spearman(log pi_hat_marginal, held-out sampled frequency), per model
entries.definition: Pre-registered pass bar: median rho over targets >= 0.5, for EVERY model (12 checkpoints spanning base/corpus_sft/rs_sft/e3/e3c and 3 checkpoints each of gdpo_v3/phase12/e1).
entries.note: Locates the '0.59 to 0.68 median Spearman across 12 models' figure the audit draft quoted without a source file: min 0.5913 (phase12_ckpt200), max 0.6761 (rs_sft), all 12 clear the 0.5 bar -- gate PASSES. This is the SAME K=8-trace marginal estimator the tail-calibration check later showed is biased low by up to ~1.7Mx in its lowest probability decade: G1 only certifies rank-correlation with sampled frequency in the estimator's bulk, not calibration in the tail, so the gate passing and the tail being badly biased are not in tension with each other.
